newsitem.title: INDIA: India's IBP, Caltex to build LPG plant.
newsitem.headline: India's IBP, Caltex to build LPG plant.

text.p: IBP Caltex, a joint venture between India's IBP Co Ltd and U.S.-based Caltex Oil Corp, will build a $50 million LPG infrastructure project in Haldia port in eastern India, senior company officials said on Wednesday.

"This facility, to be constructed over the next two years and commissioned in the first quarter of 1999, will be for the import, storage and distribution of LPG," Caltex spokesman Richard Fernie told a news conference in Calcutta.
He said the company had earmarked $500 million for investment opportunities in India. He did not say over what period of time the investments would be made.
"Caltex is keen to contribute to foreign direct investment in India," said Fernie, who is also the vice-president of Caltex Petroleum Corp, jointly owned by Texaco Inc and Chevron Corp.
He said the plant would be capable of handling up to 700,000 tonnes a year.
John Banner, managing director of IBP Caltex Ltd, said the project would have a debt-to-equity ratio of 1.5:1.
"Some foreign banks have shown very positive response for financing the project," Banner said, declining to give details.
The chairman of the joint venture, Shiv Mathur, said the ground work for the project will start in four months, after clearance from various government departments is obtained.
"The project is a demonstration of U.S. interest in India, particularly in eastern India," said U.S. ambassador to India Frank Wisner, who was at the news conference.
